10158808.note: Kept the traced dirt loop round Sites 1 to 10 and added the dirt road northwest toward the lake with its branch north to Site 13, the track across the flat past Site 12 to Site 11, the spur up to 12 and a second track north into the flat, all on the visible dirt. Every site now has a drawn road; the walkways inside the loop aren't drawn.

10161359.note: The loops follow the visible dirt lanes along the river, and Sites 1 to 11 sit on the bare pads beside them.

10180083.note: The road round the gravel lot follows what shows, and Sites 01 to 10 line the west edge of the lot and 11 to 17 the pull-ins on the east side.

10191054.note: The check doesn't draw it: both sites are on one spot under full canopy by the road, and nothing shows.

255180.note: The loops follow the visible pavement along the river. Traced the paved and gravel pull-ins to Sites 1, 2, 7, 12, 15, 19, 22, 26 to 32; the sites among the junipers east of the south loop (11, 18, 20, 21, 23 to 25) and 3, 5, 6, 8 and 13 still sit 15 to 40 m off the drawn roads where no plain pull-in shows.

262702.note: The lidar intensity shows the site's gravel lanes as plain dark bands under the firs. Redrew the lane past 001 and round the west side past 003 and 004 on its band (the photo trace ran up to 10 m west) and added the lower lane from there east past 007, 008 and 010 back up to the top lane by 011 and 012, replacing the old spur; every site is within 40 m of a road. The short spurs toward 005 and 006 aren't drawn.

272246.note: Unchanged. Zoomed on a 5 m grid, the north loop's gravel shows round 018 to 021 (the drawn Census loop runs 20 to 40 m west and south of it), but the loop's west side by 023 to 030, the dirt road south past 010 and the lanes to 002 to 009 among the pines show only as faint pale streaks on the photo, so every road couldn't be placed to 3 m and no replace was made. Site 031 still sits alone 300 m south by the day-use area.

273309.note: The survey is sparse (1.27 ground points per m²) with large gaps under the firs: the relief shows the county road and the campground lane past 2 and 15 roughly where they're drawn, but the loop by 10 and 11 and the lane past 3 to 5 fall mostly in the gaps and the intensity is noise, so they can't be checked to 3 m. Nothing traced.

274288.note: Unchanged. Zoomed on a 5 m grid, the campground is an open graded gravel flat with no lanes marked across it: 01 to 14 sit round its edges, 15 to 19 along a 25 m wide gravel strip by the shore, and 20 to 26 in a row on bare ground 60 m west. With no lane to follow, nothing was traced, and no road reaches any of the 26 sites.

251911.note: The loops follow the visible pavement through the junipers, and the Willow, Juniper and Cottonwood group sites sit inside their loops.

10046933.note: The lane along the river follows the photo's road and sites 5 to 25 sit on it; the lidar intensity shows the highway plainly but the campground lane only faintly through the oaks. No lane shows to 1 to 3 north of the west end; only 3 is more than 40 m from a road. Nothing traced.

10046989.note: The road and the earlier traced spurs to 1 to 4 follow the gravel the photo shows; the lidar intensity shows the lanes only faintly against the light gravel and grass, but agrees with them. Nothing new traced.

10047913.note: Snow and conifers: the loop is plausible and Sites 7 to 16 and 22 to 32 sit near it, but 1, 2, 4, 6, 17, 18, 20, 33, 34 and 36 sit 25 to 50 m off it, and the spurs can't be seen under the snow and trees. Sites 38 to 44 at the south loop fit; one site has no point.

10077501.note: Unchanged. Units 1 to 6 sit 40 to 200 m north of the drawn loop along a narrow dirt track and footpaths through the meadow and pines, which look like the walk-in routes from the trailhead parking, not roads, so nothing was traced and no unit has a drawn road.

10110742.note: Unchanged. Zoomed on a 5 m grid and over the lidar relief, the lane from the entrance southwest past 001 to 006 shows only in pieces between the pines, and the relief shows two parallel cuts 10 m apart there, so it couldn't be placed to 3 m; 001 to 016 still have no drawn road. 018 to 020 sit by the drawn east loop.

10114392.note: Replaced the Census road, whose north end ran down the middle of the woods: traced the dirt lane along the shore from the south past 002 and 003 to the clearing by 004 and on past 005 to 007, the spur to 002, and the track along the meadow edge. 008 to 011 in the north (four of ten) still have no drawn road, their lanes hidden under the pines, so it stays held.

10165706.note: Unchanged. Sites 01 to 26 are walk-to sites under full fir canopy: 10 to 13 and 15 to 22 sit 30 to 80 m inside the drawn loop and 01 to 08 sit 40 to 60 m east of the forest road toward the river, and no lane or path shows to any of them, so nothing could be traced. Only 31 to 37 by the paved loop and the group site fit.

10334099.note: The loops follow the visible red dirt roads in the open, and every site sits at the end of its visible spur; Group Sites A to C sit by their loops.

10364846.note: The lidar intensity shows the lanes plainly under the firs, and the Forest Service loops past 01 to 03 and 09 to 15 follow them within a few meters. Redrew the south loop past 04, 05, 07 and 08 on its band and dropped the drawn lines south-west to 06 and along the south edge, which follow no band; 06 and 13 are now the only sites more than 40 m from a road.

10364920.note: Sites spread over 1.2 km on a forested slope: 01 and 02 at the top with no road, 04 to 11 west of the drawn loop under trees, 08 and 12 alone in the open. It looks like several dispersed spots, not one campground, and most have no drawn road.

10364954.note: The lidar intensity shows every lane as a plain dark band under the firs, and the drawn roads ran up to 10 m off them; replaced them all on the bands: the loop past 10 to 22, the lane past 04 to 01, the lane south past 05 to 09 and the forest road. Only 14, in the north, is more than 40 m from a road; one site has no point.

10364992.note: The lidar relief shows the lane past 3 to 10 as a flat graded band under the trees, with the turnaround by 9 and 10, and the drawn lane follows it; the intensity shows little against the bright ground. Site 2 sits on a terrace east of the lane with no lane showing to it, and is the only site more than 40 m from a road. Nothing traced.

10365011.note: Unchanged. Zoomed on a 5 m grid, the drawn roads sit on the visible gravel round the meadow, and no lane shows toward the sites that sit off them: 01, 13 and 14 sit 15 to 20 m off on open meadow, 04, 11 and 12 under the firs at the edge, and 07 at the end of a faint track that wasn't traced.

10365026.note: The lidar relief shows Sinlahekin Road and the campground lane as graded bands under the trees, and both were drawn off them; moved the road onto its band (it ran 12 to 15 m south-west) and redrew the lane from the road past 4, 2 and 3 (it ran up to 12 m west). Site 1 sits 100 m west in the trees with no lane, one of the four sites.

10373422.note: The lidar relief shows the lakeside lane, its loops and the highway as graded bands under the firs, and the drawn roads follow them. No lanes show among the sites on the slope between the lane and the highway (06, 09, 10, 12, 15 to 17), which are reached on foot or by short pull-ins; only 15 to 17 (3 of 19) are more than 40 m from a road. Nothing traced.

10377487.note: Full canopy: the lane and its turnaround match the gap in the trees and Sites 1 and 3 sit on them, but 2 and 4 sit 20 to 25 m off them where nothing shows.

10377492.note: Full canopy: the lane through the firs is plausible and Sites 1, 3, 5 and 6 sit near it, but 2, 4 and 7 sit 25 to 60 m off it and nothing shows.

10377502.note: Unchanged. The loop by 01 to 05 is under full fir canopy on the photo, and the lidar here shows the treetops, not the ground, so no lane there can be placed and a full replace isn't possible. By 06 to 09 the visible gravel lane runs from the highway northwest to the pad by 07 with a branch north past 09, 5 to 10 m east of the drawn lane, which cuts across the trees.

10377515.note: The drawn ring is twice the size of the visible gravel turnaround and its north half runs through the trees; Sites 1 and 2 sit 25 to 30 m outside it. Site 3 across the highway sits by the end of the drawn lane, on a clearing.

10377519.note: Traced the short dirt lane to Sites 2 and 3 and the restroom. Site 1 (one of three) still has no road: its lane to the west only partly shows under the trees.

10377523.note: Full canopy: the Forest Service lane is plausible and Sites 01 to 09 sit near it, but 10 to 13 sit 20 to 50 m west of it, and nothing shows under the firs.

10377551.note: Unchanged. The road round the lake follows the gaps in the firs and Sites 01 to 09 sit beside it; 10 sits 15 m east of the loop and 11 by the north road. Under the canopy only short pieces of the spurs west of 01 and 02 show, too little to trace, and one site has no point.

10377563.note: Unchanged. Zoomed on a 5 m grid, the loop round the meadow sits on the visible gravel and 10 to 20 sit by it, but 02 to 09 to the east (eight of twenty) sit under the firs and along the far edge of the east meadow, where only a faint track shows, too vague to trace, so they still have no drawn road.

10377584.note: Unchanged. The photo shows the gravel only by 4 and 5 in the northeast and in pieces by 2 and 3, where it runs 10 m north of the drawn loop; the rest of the loop (past 9, 8 and 7 and down the west side by 1) is under full fir canopy, and the lidar relief there is mostly treetops, so the loop can't be placed to 3 m and wasn't replaced. Sites 1 to 3, 5, 6 and 9 still sit 20 to 40 m off the drawn road.

10377594.note: The lane off the highway follows the visible gravel to the clearing with Sites 1 to 3, and on to the turnaround by 4 and 5.

10377600.note: Unchanged. The drawn road still stops short of the campground: Sites 1 to 5 sit along a dirt lane through the firs that shows only in gaps (the pull-out by 2, the clearing by 3), and the lidar relief here is treetops, so the lane couldn't be placed and none of the sites has a drawn road.

10405307.note: The lidar intensity shows a light gravel clearing under the trees running from the drawn turnaround ring south to the three sites, and the relief shows the lane from the forest road to that ring where it's drawn. All three sites sit 10 to 25 m from the ring, across the open gravel; no separate lane shows. Nothing traced.

10405311.note: Replaced the source roads: the road along the lake is kept on the gaps in the firs, and the loop south of 04, drawn 4 to 7 m outside the lane, is retraced on the ring the lidar relief shows round its knoll. Sites 01 to 04 sit just west of the road where pull-outs show, and 05 just south of the loop; the photo is coarse here.

10405323.note: Unchanged. The roads follow the visible gravel between the highway and the lake, and Sites 01 to 06 and 08 to 15 sit beside them. Zoomed on a 5 m grid, 07 sits 10 m south of the east lane under the firs with no spur showing, so nothing was traced.

10405359.note: Unchanged. The lane follows the visible gravel along the ridge and Sites 04 to 06 sit on it. 01 to 03, 07 and 08 sit 15 to 30 m off it on short spurs that show only as pale patches between the firs, too broken to trace, and 09 sits west of the drawn ring.

10406480.note: The check doesn't draw it: each pole holds several sites on one spot (Pole 1 to 20, 57 sites in all). The poles line the two rows of the snowy lot, but one drawn line runs between the rows rather than on the lot's lanes.

231921.note: Unchanged. Zoomed on a 5 m grid, the loops sit on the visible dirt lanes and most sites beside them; the spurs to 003, 015 to 017, 024 to 026 and the others are 10 to 25 m pull-ins whose ends fade into the sage and aspen, not plain enough to trace to 3 m. Five sites have no point.

231948.note: The paved loops follow the visible pavement and every site sits at its pull-through or beside the loop; 2425, 3132 and 3536 are double sites in the middle.

232040.note: The road follows the visible gravel down the slope (along its east edge, about 3 m off the middle) and Sites 001, 004 to 006 and 009 sit beside it. Traced the pull-ins east to 005 and south to 010; 002, 003, 007 and 008 still sit 20 to 40 m off it among the trees, where the spurs fade.

232043.note: The survey is coarse (1.84 ground points per m²): the relief shows the bench the group sites sit on and the intensity a faint smooth band crossing it south of the drawn Forest Service road, but neither shows a lane plainly enough to check the drawn road to 3 m. Group Sites A and B sit 10 to 20 m from it. Nothing traced.

232047.note: Unchanged. Zoomed on a 5 m grid round 054 to 059, the drawn lanes sit on the visible pavement, and the pull-ins to the off-road sites (058, 057, 004, 007, 008 and the others named before) are 10 to 25 m pieces broken by pine crowns and shadow, not plain enough to trace to 3 m.

232055.note: The lidar intensity shows the campground road through the middle as a smooth band where it's drawn, within a few meters, matching the photo's gravel; under the oaks the loops past 015 to 020 and 029 to 040 show only mottled ground, so they stand on the photo alone. Group Sites A and B sit off the drawn roads in clearings. Nothing traced.

232218.note: Unchanged: the earlier trace of the paved lane south from the lot and its pull-ins to 008 and 010 to 014 sits on the visible pavement. 009 sits west of the lane with no visible pull-in, and the narrow tracks running southwest from 011 look like trails, not roads, so they weren't traced.

232227.note: Unchanged. Zoomed on a 5 m grid by A02 and A03, the off-loop group sites sit 20 to 40 m from the parking pads on the drawn loops, joined by narrow paths, not lanes (A02's is a faint footpath), so nothing was traced; the loops follow the visible gravel and the other A, B, C and E sites sit at their pull-ins.

232309.note: Cabin 2 sits beside the north lane and Cabin 1 by the building off the east lane; both lanes follow the visible gravel.

232371.note: The lidar relief shows the campground loop as a ditched lane under the pines, and the drawn loop follows it within a few meters; the intensity shows it faintly. Sites 008 to 013, 016 and 018 sit 20 to 35 m outside it, where the relief shows only faint tracks, but every site is within 40 m of the loop. Nothing traced.

232398.note: The check doesn't draw it: all four sites are on one spot on a forested slope, 80 m from the only road, with nothing visible.

232803.note: Unchanged. Zoomed on a 5 m grid, the east cluster (04, 05, 08, 14, 16, 17 and 23 to 35) sits under the pines and in the willows at the meadow edge with no lane or track showing, and the loop west of the road is under full canopy, so nothing could be traced; nearly half the sites still have no drawn road.

232804.note: The check doesn't draw it: 8 of 11 sites share points (FS1-301 to 409 shown). The small drawn loop sits on the visible gravel, and the points line its east side.

232811.note: Unchanged. The photo shows the gravel lane past 008 to 001 and the lane by 009 and 012 only in pieces between the pines, and over the lidar relief the lanes inside the loop show only as faint arcs that can't be followed, so the roads couldn't all be replaced to 3 m. The west lane still crosses the trees diagonally, and 013, 014, 020 and 021 sit 20 to 40 m from any drawn road.

232814.note: Unchanged. Zoomed on a 5 m grid and over the lidar relief, the north lane past 025 to 013 shows (gravel by 025 and 019, a crowned line in the relief at about the sites' row) and the south lane runs 5 to 6 m south of the drawn loop past 003, but where either joins the access roads, at the west end and the east end by 008 and 010, is under full canopy and doesn't show in the relief, so the loop wasn't replaced. The north sites (012, 014, 016, 019, 021 to 023, 025) still sit 20 to 40 m north of the drawn road.

232817.note: Unchanged. Thirty-odd sites are still crammed inside a small outline on an open slope of brush and rock with no pads showing, beside a paved loop that holds none of them, and 009 sits alone 330 m east; nothing on the photo shows where any one of them belongs, so none was moved, and two have no point.

232823.note: Still held: the lidar relief (16 ground points per m²) shows no road to Sites 01 to 04, which sit 300 to 600 m north on the burned slope among drainage gullies, and no lanes round 05 to 09 beyond the drawn ring by the meadow. More than half the sites have no road. Nothing traced.

232839.note: Unchanged. The lanes toward the river (003 to 016, 022 to 025) show only in short pieces between the snags and their shadows, and the lidar relief here shows the brush, not the ground, so they couldn't be traced; the drawn lane still runs through the middle of the flat, 30 to 60 m east of the sites.

232842.note: Unchanged. Zoomed on a 5 m grid, the gravel loop shows plainly south of the drawn ring and its lane runs on southeast past 008 and 005 and south through the trees, but where that lane meets the highway can't be seen under the firs, and 012 to 022 north and west of the loop sit in brush with no lane at all, so a full replace would still leave most sites with no drawn road and wasn't made.

232843.note: Unchanged. Under the snags and their long shadows no lane shows on the photo, and the lidar relief here is canopy rather than ground, so nothing could be traced; the drawn ring still sits in the trees west of the sites, and 004 to 011 sit 20 to 60 m east of it toward the river with no road.

232846.note: The loop follows the visible pavement and 007 to 009 sit beside it. Traced the west lane past 001 and 002; 004 to 006 sit 20 to 30 m south of the loop, reached on footpaths (walk-in sites).

232847.note: Unchanged (the earlier trace of the lane northeast past 002 kept). Zoomed on a 5 m grid, the loop sits on the visible gravel, but west of it the gravel pads by 009 and 007 and by 008 show no lane joining them to the loop or the highway, and 005 and 006 sit in the brush under the snags; 005 to 010 (nearly half the sites) still have no drawn road.

232851.note: Still held: neither lidar layer shows a lane through Loop C (C002 to C017); the intensity is mottled under the trees and the relief's sharp lines there are creek channels, so C002 to C014 stay 40 to 150 m from the one drawn lane. The highway shows plainly where it's drawn. Nothing traced.

232879.note: Unchanged. Groups 2 and 3 sit on open meadow and Manzanita in the trees north of it with no track showing to any of them, and the Census road across the meadow doesn't show on the photo either, so nothing could be traced; only Group 1 is near a drawn road.

232909.note: The check doesn't draw it: Sites A, C, D, E and F share one spot on the drawn road and G sits beside them; B is 60 m east in the trees. The points don't place the sites.

233218.note: The lidar intensity shows the campground road as a plain dark band under the pines; redrew it from the north edge past 05 to 08 and round the loop past 09, 13, 15 and 10 on its band (the drawn road ran 10 to 20 m east and its loop well outside the lane). Every site is within 40 m of a road; 11, 12, 14 and 16 to 18 sit in the trees 20 to 35 m off the loop with no lane showing.

233325.note: Unchanged: the earlier trace of the gravel drive west to Hillside Cabin and its branch south to Lakeside Cabin sits on the visible gravel. Zoomed on a 5 m grid, the drive's east end runs on southeast into the trees at the frame's edge, so where it meets the county road still can't be seen and the map doesn't join them.

233327.note: The loop follows the visible gravel and most sites sit at the ends of its pull-ins. 002, 006, 007, 010, 012, 014, 016, 017, 019 to 021, 027, 028, 031 and GS2 sit 20 to 50 m off it at pull-ins that show and aren't drawn, and the diagonal drawn by 024 doesn't show.

233340.note: The lidar survey covers only two strips of this frame (the creek north of 06 to 13 and a hillside south of 33), so the lanes past 14 to 38 lie outside it; where it reaches 06 to 12 the intensity is noise and the relief shows only the creek banks. The Forest Service lanes can't be checked. Nothing traced.

233787.note: Unchanged. The lane follows the gravel that shows between the firs, and Sites 004, 006 and 008 sit on it; 005, 007, 009 and 010 sit 10 to 25 m west of it at pull-outs that show only as patches between the long tree shadows, too broken to trace.

233847.note: The two loops follow the visible gravel and most sites sit at their pull-ins. Traced the gravel lane southeast from the north loop's south bend past 017 and the spur east from the loop toward 021; 005, 007, 008, 016, 018, 020 and 022 still sit 20 to 50 m off the drawn roads on pads with no plain lane to them.

234107.note: The lidar intensity shows the gravel lanes as plain dark bands. Redrew the lane west past 005 and 004 on its band and added the turnaround loop by 002 and 003 at its end, and replaced the road's end with the turnaround circle by 014 and 015; the earlier photo traces past 007 and to 006 are kept. Every site is within 40 m of a road; one site has no point.

234543.note: The lidar intensity and relief show the outer campground road plainly under the pines, and it's drawn on its band. The inner loops among 01 to 10 and 11 to 16 show only as faint grey traces in the intensity and not at all in the relief, so the drawn Forest Service loops there can't be checked to 3 m. Nothing traced.

234545.note: The lane follows the visible gravel down from the highway and Sites 003, 004, 007, 009, 010, 012 and 016 sit on it. Traced the dirt spur east to the pad by 001 and 002; 005, 006, 008, 011 and 013 to 015 still sit 15 to 30 m off the lane at pull-ins broken up by the firs.

234553.note: Unchanged. The paved loops and the lane west toward 02 show plainly, but the six group sites sit 40 to 120 m from them on open ground among the junipers with no pad, spur or track under any of them (00 north, 01 south, 02 and 03 west, 05 and 06 east), so tracing the loops wouldn't give any site a road, and the points themselves look misplaced; left untraced.

234650.note: Still held: the drawn Census rings follow nothing on either lidar layer. The intensity shows narrow dark tracks under the redwoods (one past 27 to 30, one past 09 to 11, one past 22 and 24, and a curve past 14 to 17), but they are 2 to 3 m wide, break off and don't join the highway or each other, so they can't be told from footpaths and aren't traced; 34 to 40 sit in the open south with no lane.

251357.note: Replaced the Forest Service lanes, which cut across the clearing, with a trace of the visible gravel: the entrance from the highway, the west loop and its north lane east past 009, the south lane past 001, the small east loop round the log pile, and pull-ins to 015, 013, 012, 008, 004, 005, 006, 007 and 002. Every site now sits within about 20 m of a drawn lane; 003 sits in the grass south of the main lane with no pull-in.

251940.note: Full canopy: the lanes are plausible where gaps show, and 09 sits on the visible lot, but 02 to 07 sit 25 to 60 m off any drawn road under the firs.

252035.note: Full canopy: the lane is plausible and Sites 002 to 005 and 007 sit near it, but 001, 003 and 006 sit 20 to 30 m off any drawn road, and nothing shows under the pines.

267076.note: Unchanged. Only the county road is drawn; Sites 01 to 12 sit 60 to 150 m east of it among the pines and snags toward the river, and no lane or track to them shows on the photo, so nothing could be traced.

267077.note: Unchanged. Zoomed on a 5 m grid, the red dirt between the pines east of the loops shows only as separate patches by 05 and below 20, not a lane that can be followed, so nothing was traced; 02 to 07, 09, 13, 15 to 21 still sit 20 to 50 m off the drawn loops (a third or more of the sites), and one site has no point.

267558.note: The lidar intensity shows the campground loop and the road in as plain dark bands under the pines, and the drawn loop sits on them, with the pull-in spurs to 002, 003, 005, 007, 010, 011, 012, 013 and 014 branching off it; every site is within 40 m of the loop. The spurs aren't drawn. Nothing traced.

273758.note: Unchanged. Zoomed on a 5 m grid, the loops follow the dirt lanes among the oaks and junipers (the north loop's east side under the trees doesn't show), and the pull-ins to 001, 003, 005, 008, 010 and 012 are 10 to 25 m pieces broken by the crowns, too short and vague to trace.

10004932.note: The lidar layers are too coarse here (1.62 ground points per m², steep rocky ground): the highway shows, but neither the intensity nor the relief shows the campground lanes, so the drawn lanes past 1 to 7 and to 8 can't be checked. Nothing traced.

10044761.note: Replaced the source roads with a full trace: the loops, the entrance and the highway now sit on the visible gravel and pavement, and the northeast lane past 93 to 97 and 117 to 120, which ran 6 to 10 m east through the pines, is on its gravel. Many sites still sit 20 to 40 m off the lanes at the ends of pull-ins that aren't drawn (84, 86, 90, 92, 109, 111, 100, 103, 105 in the northwest; 33, 46, 50, 68 elsewhere).

10190967.note: Replaced the Park Service road with a trace on the visible dirt: Navy Road through the junction north of the camp, the wide road west from it, the lane south past 007, 003 and 004 and on southwest past 006, and the spur east to 001. Every site now sits within about 20 m of a drawn lane; the short paths to 005 and 006 among the oaks aren't drawn.

232460.note: Unchanged. Zoomed on a 10 m grid over the northeast loops (001 to 061), the ground between the pines is bare dirt throughout and the long tree shadows cut across it, so the lanes can't be told from the open ground or placed to 3 m; the drawn rings still cross the trees and 037 to 040, 043, 047, 049, 012 and 015 sit 20 to 50 m off them.

232465.note: The 2008 survey has only 0.4 ground points per m² under the old-growth firs: the relief shows the highway and the river terraces but none of the campground's lanes, and the intensity is noise, so Loops A to H can't be checked. Nothing traced.

249982.note: Unchanged. Under the oaks the photo shows only the clearings by 18 to 25, and the lidar relief shows terraced pads but no lane that can be followed, so the ring couldn't be replaced; Sites 02 and 04 to 12 along the north side (more than a third) still sit 20 to 60 m outside the drawn ring with no road.

272266.note: Unchanged. The Park Service loops follow the visible pavement and most sites sit on pads beside them. Zoomed on a 5 m grid, B 36 to B 45 east of the drawn lane sit along sandy footpaths through the brush, not lanes, so nothing was traced; A 66, B 01 and B 05 still sit between loops, and one site has no point.

10327316.note: The loops follow the visible pavement (the west side drawn a few metres east of it), and Sites W03, W07 to W18 sit beside them. W02 and W04 to W06 sit on the lawn inside the loop, likely walk-in sites, with no road.

233437.note: Unchanged. Zoomed on a 5 m grid along the shore, B077 to B093 sit on open grass and among the oaks between the drawn south road and the water with no lane or track showing, and B057 to B062 in the north sit under the oaks where only faint tracks show, so nothing could be traced; nearly half the sites still sit 20 to 60 m from any drawn road.

270421.note: A boat-in campground, so no roads, as expected. Sites 001 to 030 sit on the pale cleared pads that ring the grove on the point.
